lessonRef.title: Unit assessment: indirect measurement of inaccessible lengths

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Unit assessment. Work alone, show your steps, and check your work before you finish.

items.prompt: A 3 m pole casts a 3 m shadow. At the same moment a building casts a 6 m shadow. How tall is the building?
choices: 7 m
5 m
2 m
6 m

items.prompt: Two triangles with all three pairs of sides in the same ratio are similar. Which statement correctly justifies it?
choices: The criterion holds only when the ratio is a whole number.
Equal ratios of sides guarantee congruence, not similarity.
This is the SSS similarity criterion: a dilation matches one triangle’s sides to the other’s, and the resulting figures are congruent.
This is the SSS congruence criterion applied directly.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF. Side AB = 4 corresponds to DE = 8. If BC = 6, find EF.
In a right triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse divides it into segments of length 6 and 24. Find the altitude.
A 5 m pole casts a 4 m shadow. At the same moment a building casts a 16 m shadow. How tall is the building?
A line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally. Which statement correctly justifies it?
choices: The parallel line creates corresponding angles, giving a smaller triangle similar to the original by AA, so the sides are in proportion.
The result follows from the Pythagorean theorem applied twice.
The two parts of each side are congruent because the line is parallel.
The parallel line bisects both sides by definition.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF. Side AB = 7 corresponds to DE = 21. If BC = 11, find EF.
In a right triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse divides it into segments of length 7 and 7. Find the altitude.
A 5 m pole casts a 2 m shadow. At the same moment a building casts a 16 m shadow. How tall is the building?
choices: 6 m

items.prompt: The Pythagorean theorem can be proved using similarity. Which statement correctly justifies it?
choices: The altitude to the hypotenuse creates two triangles similar to the original; writing both similarity proportions and adding them yields a² + b² = c².
The theorem follows because all right triangles are similar to each other.
The theorem follows from the triangle inequality.
Similarity gives a² + b² = c² only for isosceles right triangles.
